one_month_reasoning: No earnings fall inside 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-31: AppLovin reported Q3 on Nov 5 in 2025 and Nov 6 in 2024, and third-party calendars put Q3 2026 at Nov 4-11. The Q3 guide ($2.055-2.085B revenue, 7-8% QoQ) and consensus ($2.07B) match, so the guide sets no pre-announcement trap. Things inside the window: the earnings-date announcement; sell-side alt-data notes on e-commerce merchant sign-ups (a BofA note like this cost 13% in one day on Jul 13); more law-firm releases ahead of the Nov 16 lead-plaintiff deadline (noise, already known); Meta Horizon follow-ups; and macro. The stock just fell 9.5% in a week to a new 52-week low ($275.13 intraday), so short-term reversal and negative momentum roughly cancel. I therefore use a near-symmetric lognormal centred on $280 with monthly sigma 21% (75%/3.5) and no directional call.

fair_value.method: Blend of 50% P/E (NTM EPS at Oct-2027 ~$23 x 17x = $391) and 50% FCF yield (NTM FCF ~$7.2B at a 6% yield on ~322M shares = $373). Net debt (~$0.46B) is immaterial.

inputs_detail.derivation: Alpha Vantage mean of 27 analysts; was $21.16 60 days ago and 19 of 24 revisions in the last 30 days were cuts, so I take the mean as given and add no premium

FY27 $20 grown 20%. That is below management's 'roughly 30% annually' long-term revenue compounding (call) and consensus FY27 revenue growth of 27%; I cut it for slower model gains (Q2: 'lighter than normal') and add ~4% per share from buybacks ($1.8B authorisation left, ~$1B/quarter pace in Q1)

Today the stock trades ~14x FY27 consensus ($281/$20) and ~15x NTM. Mega-cap ad platforms trade around 20-22x. 17x sits between the two: it assumes some re-rating if growth holds near 25-30%, but less than the analyst targets (mean cut from ~$654 to ~$498) imply

bear.story: Model gains stay lumpy, so gaming (still the core) slows sharply. E-commerce self-serve (Ads Manager GA late June 2026) scales slowly because generative video creative is still missing. AI or Meta tooling squeezes the mobile UA wedge. FY27 EPS lands ~$16 (the low end of consensus) and the stock de-rates to ~11x NTM EPS of ~$17.

base.story: Revenue grows ~25-30% in 2027 and EBITDA margin holds ~82-84%. FY27 EPS is ~$19-20 and buybacks continue at $1B+/quarter. The multiple recovers only partly, to ~15x an NTM EPS of ~$22.

bull.story: The post-Q2 model step-up ('Q3 off to a strong start') compounds. Consumer/e-commerce advertisers scale beyond the mid-market through partners like Triple Whale, and video creative ships. FY27 EPS reaches ~$22.5 (the high end of consensus) and the stock re-rates to ~19x NTM EPS of ~$27.

thesis_break_reason: $175 is under 9x FY27 consensus EPS and ~10x 2026 EPS for a business with 80%+ EBITDA margins and near-zero capex. At that price the market would be pricing a structural earnings decline, not de-rating: for example, sequential revenue declines from Axon model degradation, a platform policy shock (Apple/Google/Meta), loss of a major demand partner, or a material adverse turn in the litigation or regulatory matters. Ordinary volatility at 60-75% vol puts this level about one standard deviation down, so a sustained trade there would need fundamental confirmation that I would treat as the break.

key_uncertainties: Whether Axon model gains resume a steady cadence (management: 'no guarantee... lifts in every single period of three months')
The pace of e-commerce/consumer advertiser scaling. Ads Manager went GA in late June 2026, but management says creative tooling is the biggest hurdle
The durability of an ~84% EBITDA margin as training and inference compute costs rise (~$0.10 compute per incremental revenue dollar)
Whether the de-rating to ~14x forward EPS persists or worsens. Revision momentum is negative (FY27 EPS mean down from $21.16 to $20.00 in 60 days)

reasoning: Primary documents show a business still compounding fast. Q2 2026 revenue was $1.924B (+53%) with an 83.9% adj. EBITDA margin and $3.76 GAAP EPS. The Q3 guide of $2.055-2.085B (+46-48%) explicitly excludes unreleased model improvements. Net debt is ~$0.46B and $1.8B of buyback authorisation was left at Jun 30. The 10-Q shows why Q2 FCF dipped to $863M: H1 cash taxes were $640M vs $101M a year earlier, a timing effect, not a business one. Q2 net revenue per install rose 58% while installs fell 2%, so growth remains price/performance-led. The market has de-rated the stock from $673.82 at year-end to $281 (~14x FY27 consensus EPS of $20). The drivers were AI-disruption fears (February), a BofA e-commerce sign-up datapoint (July), the slight Q2 revenue miss with 'lighter than normal' model gains (August), and a class action plus Meta's Horizon tools (September). Insiders show no open-market buying: August Form 4s are tax-withholding only, at $308.77. Valuation of P/E 17x on ~$23 NTM EPS ($391) blended with a 6% FCF yield ($373) gives ~$382 fair value 12 months out. I do not put the median there, because estimate revisions are falling, momentum is sharply negative (new lows this week) and the de-rating can persist. The scenario mix of 30% bear at $180, 45% base at $330 and 25% bull at $510 gives a mean of ~$330. I fit a lognormal with median ~$300 and sigma 0.58: forward vol is below the 75% realized, which included three 15-20% event gaps. I thickened the far left tail slightly for business-break risk. Research went mostly to SEC filings and call transcripts; consensus came from Alpha Vantage, and option data was deliberately not consulted.
